bet.text: One centrally located pivoting mechanism that intakes, shoots and scores the amp, kept away from other robots and field elements.

demand.text: Objectives were chosen at kickoff: the speaker, the amp, and fast movement around other robots. They expected more high-speed collisions, so the intake had to be reliable and need little repair. The trap was a long-term aim, helpful but not the most important task.

auto.text: Consistency comes first. Tuning goes in steps: single modules, path following without correction, odometry, then vision. Routines are built from pieces by a procedural method, with about 74,000 or more combinations, so they can work with partners and against opponents.

cycle.text: With the arm down the note comes in under the raised bumper and runs along polycord into the shooter. Raised part way it shoots the speaker; fully up it scores the amp.
A post credits 1771's accuracy as a feeder, dropping notes between the amp and the subwoofer from the center line.

endgame.text: A 'chameleon' climber built on carbon fiber boat hooks lifts the robot high enough for the arm to score the trap.

gave_up.text: The robot was not built around the trap; that had to wait until a climber could lift it to the right height.

changed.text: The first climber, a motor and spool alone, was not sturdy at Gwinnett in week 3. Before Albany in week 5 they tried other spools, added a constant-force spring and improved the intake, then climbed and trapped in many matches.
In the Gwinnett finals the team first suspected a beam break wire, traced a fault to the RoboRIO, skipped a match to fix it and fitted a spare.

outcome.text: 58-7-0 in official play; ranked 18 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 52.78, Daly).

facts.text: Modules are tuned to follow speed and rotation before any path work

solves.text: Stay reliable through high-speed collisions and rarely need repair

facts.text: The bumpers are raised so a note passes beneath
The lowered arm acts as part of it
Runs the note straight into the shooter

functions.name: Pivoting arm

solves.text: Cover intake, speaker and amp in one mechanism that moves smoothly

functions.type: single long arm on a high pivot

facts.text: The arm is more than a foot long
Most of the motors sit next to the pivot and long belts drive the intake end
Down for intake, part way for the speaker, fully up for amp or trap
A Kraken on each side lets it put spin on the note
A partner says it set two world-record scores in one day with 1771 as its feeder, which takes accurate placement in the corner by the amp and a fast scorer

functions.name: Chameleon climber

solves.text: Lift the robot to the height the arm needs for the trap

functions.type: carbon fiber boat hook climber with spool

facts.text: A motor and spool with constant-force spring assist
3D printed, which helped the team iterate on it

cost.text: A motor and spool alone was not sturdy, and spring force took tuning so it helped without overpowering the climber

functions.name: Wood structure
functions.type: mostly wood robot cut on a router

facts.text: A broken part can be patched by screwing on another piece of wood
A new part can be cut and ready in a couple of minutes

solves.text: Fit around partners and opponents without programming being the limit

facts.text: Upwards of about 74,000 combinations of notes and positions

decisions.because: it is easy to design around, quick to cut and easy to patch
decisions.instead_of: aluminum, where bending has to be considered

decisions.because: fast collisions were expected and the team wanted it reliable, with little repair
keeping mass near the pivot makes a long arm smooth to control
decisions.cost: long belt runs to power the intake end

decisions.because: prototypes and other teams' threads showed spin mattered for consistent shots
other climbers on offer would not lift the robot to the right height for the trap
